verdict.summary: Register an integration at launchpad.37signals.com, get a client ID and secret, and any Basecamp user can authorize it immediately: there's no review, marketplace or install cap in the docs. Classic Launchpad tokens are all-or-nothing, but a newer authorization server at app.basecamp.com (live, but not yet in the written docs) adds a read-only scope, PKCE, Dynamic Client Registration and a hosted MCP server.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Register the app (a dummy redirect URI is accepted), run the authorization code flow, call authorization.json to find the account href. No verification step is documented.

timeToProd.assumes: A standard Launchpad integration reading and writing project data with full-access tokens; the read-only path via app.basecamp.com is equally self-serve but less documented.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs describe no review or approval step. Absence of a review is our reading, not an explicit statement.

prerequisites.item: A 37signals ID (Basecamp account) to sign in to Launchpad
prerequisites.why: The integrations console redirects to sign-in, and the first test authorization needs a Basecamp account.
Required at registration; Basecamp's docs say a dummy URL like http://myapp.com/oauth works if you aren't ready yet.

prerequisites.item: A User-Agent header naming your app with a URL or email on every API request
prerequisites.why: Requests without it get 400 Bad Request.

scopeTiers.impact: Launchpad's authorize request takes no scope parameter; tokens act as the user across all their Basecamp accounts and projects. The authorization document reports scope 'full' for Basecamp-issued tokens.
app.basecamp.com advertises a read scope, and the hosted MCP server lets users pick Read-only or Full access at consent. Useful for summarising agents that shouldn't write.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Scopes observed in live metadata on 2026-10-20; the written OAuth guide doesn't document requesting them yet.

scopeTiers.impact: Needed to call the hosted MCP server at https://mcp.basecamp.com/mcp, whose 401 challenge asks for scope="mcp full".

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed in the WWW-Authenticate header on 2026-10-20.

steps.title: Sign in to Launchpad and register an integration
steps.detail: Go to the integrations console, create a new app, and enter name, company, website and redirect URI. Copy the client_id and client_secret.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Form fields beyond redirect URI weren't observed because we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://launchpad.37signals.com/authorization/new?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=... , then POST grant_type=authorization_code with client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri and code to https://launchpad.37signals.com/authorization/token. The legacy type=web_server parameter is still accepted but not recommended.

steps.title: Resolve the user's accounts
steps.detail: GET https://launchpad.37signals.com/authorization.json (or https://3.basecampapi.com/authorization.json) with the token. Pick accounts with product 'bc3' and use each account's href (https://3.basecampapi.com/{account_id}) as the API base URL.

steps.title: Add refresh handling
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 2 weeks (expires_in 1209600). POST grant_type=refresh_token with the refresh token, client_id and client_secret to the same token endpoint.

steps.title: Build API calls with User-Agent, pagination and backoff
steps.detail: Send a User-Agent with app name and contact. Follow Link rel=next headers (geared pages of 15/30/50/100). Honour 429 Retry-After (first limit is about 50 requests per 10 seconds per IP) and retry 5xx with exponential backoff.

steps.title: Optionally move to the app.basecamp.com authorization server for read-only or public clients
steps.detail: Its metadata lists authorize /oauth/authorizations/new, token /oauth/tokens, PKCE S256, device and client_credentials grants, DPoP, a registration endpoint (/oauth/clients) and client ID metadata documents, with scopes full/read/mcp/offline_access. Test carefully: this isn't yet described in the written guide.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Fetched 2026-10-20. An empty POST to /oauth/clients returned 400 invalid_redirect_uri 'redirect_uris is required', so DCR is live.

steps.title: Or connect to the hosted MCP server
steps.detail: If your agent is an MCP client, point it at https://mcp.basecamp.com/mcp. Basecamp says there's nothing to set up on its end; users sign in, pick an account and choose Read-only or Full access.

steps.title: Test with a real Basecamp account
steps.detail: Authorize the app once with your own Basecamp account and confirm projects and to-dos load.

blockers.symptom: 400 Bad Request on every API call
blockers.cause: Missing User-Agent header with app name and contact.
The authorize request is missing response_type=code (or legacy type=web_server).
blockers.fix: Add response_type=code with client_id and redirect_uri.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed with a bare GET on 2026-10-20.

blockers.cause: Dynamic rate limits; the first most clients hit is 50 requests per 10 seconds per IP.
blockers.fix: Honour Retry-After and spread requests, especially if many users share one server IP.

blockers.symptom: API calls return 404 or wrong data for some accounts
blockers.cause: The token covers several 37signals products and accounts; you're using a non-bc3 account or the identity id.
blockers.fix: Filter accounts to product 'bc3' and use the account href as the base URL; don't use identity ids in API calls.

blockers.symptom: 401 using a DPoP-bound token with 'Authorization: Bearer'
blockers.cause: Bound tokens reject the Bearer scheme.
blockers.fix: Send 'Authorization: DPoP <token>' plus a DPoP proof header.

nuances.text: Classic Launchpad tokens have no scopes: one token grants full access to everything the user can see, across all their Basecamp accounts. Use the newer read scope if your agent only reads.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No scope parameter is documented for Launchpad; the read scope comes from live app.basecamp.com metadata.

nuances.text: Basecamp advises against using its OAuth for 'Login with Basecamp' because it doesn't verify email addresses.
Accounts include an RFC 8707 resource indicator (urn:bc:account:<id>) for requesting account-scoped tokens, and DPoP-bound tokens are supported.

The API defines an 'Agent' person type for AI agents using client-credentials tokens; agents can reach only a limited set of endpoints and get 403 elsewhere. New person types may appear without a version change.
Flat routes (e.g. /todos/{id}.json) are now canonical; project-scoped /buckets/{id}/ routes are legacy but supported. The API isn't compatible with Basecamp 2 or Classic.
Rate limits are per IP, so a multi-tenant agent backend shares one budget across users unless it spreads egress.
